result:
**I'd make curiosity the default human operating system.**

Not forced kindness, not enforced equality, not some top-down utopia—those all go wrong. Just this: every single person wakes up with an *intense, almost annoying* drive to understand how things actually work. A built-in allergy to bullshit. A reflex to ask "but why?" and "what if we're wrong?" before defending their current beliefs.

Everything downstream gets better:
- Politics stops being tribal warfare and becomes iterative engineering
- Education stops being memorization and becomes actual learning
- Relationships improve because people get curious about each other instead of assuming
- Science accelerates because fewer resources are wasted on sacred cows
- Even entertainment gets smarter because audiences demand it

The beautiful part is it wouldn't feel like a change. It would feel like humanity finally waking up to what we were always supposed to be—curious apes who look at the stars and can't help but build telescopes.

Everything else we argue about (resources, power, ideology) eventually sorts itself out when enough people are genuinely trying to understand reality instead of protecting their narrative.

That's the one tweak. The rest is just debugging.
